An older page about left-handed drawing cannot establish that numerous relevant images appeared readily in that search service. The absence of an archive does not show Marcus was wrong. limitations: Historical search results may not have been preserved.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The critic's objection that the system had not been taught relevant information about left-handed drawing is nonsense, because a few seconds on Google Images turns up lots of people drawing with their left hand.
conditions: rebuttal to one critic's objection about the system

statement.excerpt: But this is nonsense; even a few seconds with Google Images supplies lots of people drawing with their left hand.
statement.document_title: Statistics versus Understanding: The Essence of What Ails Generative AI

from_speaker: lots of people drawing with their left hand
our_interpretation: The checkable observation is that an ordinary Google Images search readily returned numerous distinct depictions of people actually drawing with their left hand.
A few seconds means readily discoverable results, not a precisely timed speed test. Lots means numerous examples, not a single successful result.
Because this describes a live search service without a reporting period, the target is its observable state on the post date, February 13, 2024.
The rebuttal's separate inference about model training requires evidence of training inclusion. Public availability alone does not establish that inclusion.
criteria.support_condition: A contemporaneous archived Google Images result set or independent recorded search shows numerous visibly relevant left-handed drawing examples readily available through an ordinary query.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporaneous recorded searches show that relevant examples were scarce or not readily discoverable, contrary to the claimed abundance.
